title: Data reduction and feature generation techniques for classification algorithms on heterogenous behavioural data
tldr: A feature generation framework that uses domain-specific transformations and heterogeneous behavioural data to reduce data size while improving classification performance across financial and non-financial domains.
problem_and_motivation: In modern classification systems, data can be heterogeneous, highly redundant, and noisy. Feature engineering can improve model performance but requires domain expertise and is time-consuming. The authors propose a framework that automates domain-specific feature generation and data reduction for classification tasks on behavioural data.
approach: The framework applies domain-specific transformations (e.g., percentile-based aggregation, ratio calculations, trend features) on top of raw behavioural data. It generates three subsets: raw data, generated features only, and concatenated raw + generated features. Multiple classification models (XGBoost, CatBoost, Logistic Regression, etc.) are evaluated on real-world datasets from credit scoring, insurance, and other domains.
findings: Generated features consistently improved predictive performance over raw data alone, especially for simpler models. XGBoost with raw features performed best overall. Feature reduction techniques (percentile-based aggregation) reduced data size while maintaining or improving performance. The framework worked across diverse domains including credit scoring, insurance, and customer behavior prediction.

definitions: Heterogeneous data: Data containing multiple types (numeric, categorical) with mixed distributions
Percentile aggregation: Computing min/max values at specific percentile levels (e.g., 10th, 90th)
Data reduction: Reducing dimensionality while preserving predictive signal

topic_relevance.mapping_rationale: Core contribution is a predictive modelling framework using XGBoost, CatBoost, and other classifiers on real-world datasets
Proposes feature engineering and classification framework using modern ML algorithms (XGBoost, CatBoost, Random Forest)
Primary evaluation dataset is a credit scoring dataset from a European banking institution
Credit scoring task involves predicting loan default probability

limitations: No explicit domain adaptation or transfer learning evaluated
Only tested on relatively small datasets (up to 10K samples)
Framework relies on manual domain-specific feature definitions
No comparison with automated feature engineering tools like AutoFeat or Featuretools
Does not address concept drift or temporal changes in data distributions
remember_this: Framework transforms raw behavioural data into domain-specific features that improve classification across credit, insurance, and behavior domains. Key insight: domain-specific feature generation can reduce data requirements while maintaining performance. The concatenated (raw + generated) features often perform better than either alone.
